title: Reflection through mirrors
ques: What kind of mirror is used as a **rear-view mirror** in vehicles, and why?

answer.content:
A **convex mirror** is used as a rear-view mirror.

This is because it always produces an erect, diminished image, which provides a **much wider field of view** for the driver compared to a plane mirror, allowing them to see more of the traffic behind.

explanation: This tests the practical application of image formation rules for spherical mirrors.

title: Refraction through lenses
ques: What is the **power of a lens**, and what is its SI unit?

answer.content:
The **power of a lens** is a measure of its degree of convergence or divergence of light rays falling on it. It is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length (in meters). 
* Formula: P = 1 / f (in meters)

The SI unit of power of a lens is the **Diopter (D)**.

explanation: This defines the standard metric used in optometry to describe corrective lenses.

title: Optical instruments
ques: What is the basic difference in the construction of a **Compound Microscope** versus an **Astronomical Telescope** regarding their objective lenses?

answer.content:
* **Compound Microscope:** The objective lens has a very **short focal length** and a **small aperture** (to view tiny, nearby objects).
* **Astronomical Telescope:** The objective lens has a very **large focal length** and a **large aperture** (to gather as much light as possible from distant, faint celestial objects).

explanation: This contrasts two major optical instruments based on their intended functions and resulting designs.

title: Wave optics phenomena
ques: Briefly describe the phenomenon of **Diffraction** of light.

answer.content:
**Diffraction** is the phenomenon of the bending of light waves around the corners of an obstacle or through an aperture, and its subsequent spreading into the geometrical shadow region of the obstacle.

This effect is most pronounced when the size of the obstacle or aperture is comparable to the wavelength of the light.

explanation: This introduces a fundamental property of light that proves its wave nature.
